qualifying_findings.title: 9Router login brute-force lockout bypass via spoofable client IP header
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: 9Router before 0.5.6 uses the client-supplied X-9r-Real-Ip value as the login limiter bucket key when requests reach Next.js without the sanitizing custom server wrapper. A remote unauthenticated attacker can rotate the header to avoid the five-attempt progressive lockout on POST /api/auth/login and continue dashboard password guessing.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: decolua/9router before 0.5.6; dashboard login limiter behind deployments that trust unsanitized X-9r-Real-Ip.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An AI router holds provider configuration and paid model access; bypassing dashboard throttling weakens the administrative control plane protecting LLM credentials and routing policy.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad 9Router product context belongs upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: No general AI-development practice update required.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Identity and access control for AI router administration.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence from CVE Services, NVD, GitHub advisory, commit, and fixed release references.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, consider whether this belongs with the existing 9Router public LLM API auth-bypass page or merits a separate login-rate-limit leaf.

qualifying_findings.title: Moonshot AI Kimi Code MCP configuration loader command injection
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Moonshot AI Kimi Code through 0.31.0 has OS command injection in the MCP Configuration Loader. The CVE record says public exploit material exists and version 0.31.1 fixes both the primary untrusted .mcp.json auto-spawn path and a secondary PATH planting vector by resolving fd/stty binaries to absolute paths before confirmation.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Moonshot AI Kimi Code 0.1 through 0.31.0; fixed in 0.31.1.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Coding-agent MCP configuration is an instruction-to-tool authority boundary; untrusted workspace configuration can become command execution before or around trust prompts.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad Moonshot AI and Kimi Code product context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General coding-agent configuration hygiene may route upstream as a practice note.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Security-specific command execution and MCP configuration trust boundary stays local.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: Moderate-high confidence from CVE/NVD/VulDB and release reference; exploit details are not reproduced here and should be handled carefully during ingest.

qualifying_findings.title: mcp-toolbox-sdk-python reuses Google ID tokens across audiences
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: The toolbox-core package in mcp-toolbox-sdk-python through 1.1.0 caches Google ID tokens without keying the cache by requested audience. An application authenticating to multiple audiences in one process can send a token minted for a sensitive service to a secondary service; an attacker controlling or monitoring that secondary service can capture and replay the token against the sensitive service.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Google mcp-toolbox-sdk-python toolbox-core through 1.1.0; patch reference PR 675.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP data-tool SDKs often mediate delegated access to databases and services; audience-confused token reuse breaks least privilege across tool backends.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: General MCP Toolbox product and SDK context belongs upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General MCP SDK implementation practice may route upstream if needed.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Credential audience isolation and delegated tool access risk stays local.

qualifying_findings.title: IBM FTM AI agent server unauthenticated RAG poisoning can steer MCP tool calls
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: IBM Financial Transaction Manager for RedHat OpenShift versions 4.0.6.0 through 4.0.10.0 are vulnerable to RAG poisoning in the FTM AI agent server. An unauthenticated attacker can upsert malicious runbook content into the vector database, influencing AI-driven MCP tool calls and potentially causing unauthorized payment actions or payment-data exfiltration.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: IBM Financial Transaction Manager for RedHat OpenShift 4.0.6.0 through 4.0.10.0; FTM AI agent server api.vectordb.runbooks.js.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: This is a direct retrieval-poisoning-to-tool-action path in a financial operations agent, crossing data integrity, delegated authority, and transaction-risk boundaries.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad IBM product context belongs upstream only if a product/provider page is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General RAG poisoning practice may route upstream; this product vulnerability stays local.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: RAG integrity, tool authorization, and payment-action risk stays local.

qualifying_findings.title: Kotaemon multi-user chat handlers allow cross-user transcript access and mutation
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: Cinnamon's Kotaemon through v0.12.0 has incorrect authorization checks in four multi-user chat handler methods that load Conversation records by ID without verifying ownership. Authenticated users can read other users' chat transcripts, RAG retrieval history, AI-generated plots, and suggestions, and can delete, rename, or overwrite another user's conversation suggestions.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Cinnamon AI Kotaemon all versions up to and including v0.12.0; libs/ktem/ktem/pages/chat/control.py multi-user chat handlers.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: RAG chat systems store prompts, retrieved context, generated artifacts, and user data; broken conversation ownership exposes sensitive model context and enables cross-user manipulation.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad Kotaemon product context belongs upstream if not already present.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: General RAG application authorization practice may route upstream.
upstream_routing.local_security_lens: Data privacy and authorization boundary for RAG chat systems stays local.

qualifying_findings.title: OpenClaw iOS logs agent deep-link bearer keys to public diagnostics
qualifying_findings.concise_factual_summary: OpenClaw iOS before 2026.8.11 logs full agent deep-link URLs, including persistent bearer keys, to unified logs as public diagnostic data. Attackers who obtain diagnostic archives can recover unrotated keys and replay forged deep links to submit agent requests without local confirmation prompts.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: OpenClaw iOS before 2026.8.11; fixed by patch commit 8361f3704dd5e151ff1325e62ff5de658b6c62e6.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Mobile agent deep links are delegated-action credentials; logging bearer keys turns diagnostics into an agent-command replay channel.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Broad OpenClaw product context belongs upstream if needed.
